notes_list.title: Aldehyde and Ketone Tests
notes_list.basic_overview: Aldehydes are generally more readily oxidized than ketones and can be distinguished by classic silver-ion and copper(II) reduction tests.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Tollens reagent can oxidize aldehydes while reducing Ag(I) to metallic silver. Fehling/Benedict-type systems can be reduced by suitable aliphatic aldehydes under alkaline conditions.
notes_list.examples: RCHO → RCOO− with Tollens under alkaline aqueous conditions; ketones generally do not give the same response.
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: Aqueous alkaline medium is typical. Fresh Tollens reagent is used for qualitative testing.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: Aldehyde hydrate or related reactive form is oxidized while metal ion is reduced. The exact mechanistic picture depends on medium and substrate.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: Redox feasibility depends on thermodynamics and kinetics; complexation and pH affect the apparent test response.
notes_list.common_traps: Some α-hydroxy ketones can reduce copper reagents; therefore a positive test is not uniquely “aldehyde” in every formulation.

exam_focus.level: IIT-JAM / MSc entrance / GATE concept depth
